subject: Discovery recap + integration & PoC owners (CareOptics)
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@careoptics.com>
Cc: Rina Patel <rina.patel@careoptics.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap + integration & PoC owners (CareOptics)

Hi Tom & Rina,

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap from our side so we have shared expectations and clear owners for the PoC. Please flag anything I missed or correct timelines below.

Top pain points you called out:
- Latency variability on your current NLU pipeline (spikes during end-of-day batch processing).
- High token costs from heavy re-requests and lack of effective caching.
- Difficulty running models securely in your VPC for PHI-sensitive use cases.

Current stack / constraints:
- Model infra: internal PyTorch-based service with NVIDIA T4s in GCP.
- Orchestration: Airflow for nightly jobs; real-time inference via a small Node service fronting the model.
- Security: Must keep PHI inside VPC; SOC2 compliance required for production integrations.

Success criteria for an initial PoC (agreed):
1) Reduce median tail latency in interactive flows by 20% (95th percentile target).
2) Demonstrate >2x cost improvement per 1,000 tokens through batching + prefix caching.
3) Serve a minimal PHI workflow fully inside CareOptics VPC with KMS-managed keys.

Proposed PoC scope & timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): detailed technical kickoff, confirm SDK language and access. Owner: Jasmine (Redwood) + Tom (CareOptics).
- Week 1: integration spike — install Redwood SDK in a sandbox, validate token auth and simple generate calls. Tech owner: CareOptics backend engineer (TBD).
- Week 2–3: run performance baseline (current) and Redwood-backed baseline; iterate caching settings. Owner: Redwood SRE + CareOptics infra.
- Week 4: demo results and decide go/no-go for Dedicated capacity.

Integration specifics we need from your side (action items):
- Which SDK language does your team prefer? From call it sounded like Node for the real-time service and Python for batch jobs.
- A short list of representative prompts / request shapes (tokens, typical batch sizes).
- Access to a sandbox GCP project or SSH to a staging env for latency profiling (least privilege).

Attachments I dropped: redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf (SDK snippets for Node & Python) and a simple PoC checklist template.

Next immediate steps (this week):
- Tom: confirm the two engineers who will own the spike and share their emails by Tue EOD (Mar 23).
- Rina: share procurement contact / SOW constraints if any.
- Ben/Marissa (cc'd): can you prepare an initial reserved-capacity estimate and an internal SRE pairing plan for Week 2? I put a rough ask below — no need to finalize the quote before the technical spike.

Thanks — I'll schedule the technical kickoff once we have the two engineer contacts.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0143

--
Attachment: redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf (PDF)
--
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@careoptics.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Rina Patel <rina.patel@careoptics.com>, Procurement <procurement@careoptics.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 15:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap + integration & PoC owners (CareOptics)

Thanks Jasmine — this looks right. A couple clarifications and commitments from our side:

Clarifications:
- The Node service is the highest priority for latency (customer-facing). The Python batch is lower priority but will be part of the baseline comparables.
- For PHI, we must ensure no logs leave our VPC and that keys are customer-managed.

Commitments:
- I'll assign two engineers: Mateo Alvarez (backend lead) and Irene Choi (infra/SRE). Mateo.m@careoptics.com and irene.c@careoptics.com — they will be the tech owners on the spike.
- Procurement looped in (procurement@careoptics.com) — Rina will follow up with commercial constraints and a preliminary NDA/PO process.

For the token shapes: I'll have Mateo drop a short set of representative payloads by Tue.

One ask for Redwood: can you confirm that the SDK supports streaming responses and whether there are any additional headers we need to set for VPC private endpoints?

I'll wait for Ben/Marissa's initial capacity guidance before we schedule the Week 2 profiling window.

Tom
VP, Product Engineering | CareOptics
Tom.Reynolds@careoptics.com | +1 (617) 555-0228

- PoC goals: 20% reduction in 95th latency, >2x cost/unit improvement, VPC/KMS for PHI.
- Immediate ask: a conservative reserved-capacity estimate (small T4 pool / burst plan) and approximate monthly cost for a 4-week PoC. Also please flag any blockers for enabling private VPC endpoints with customer-managed KMS.

Suggested internal pairing plan:
- Week 1: Marissa to own SRE pairing & infra onboarding (help Mateo/Irene get sandbox access and generate keys).
- Week 2: Ben to run performance baselines & tune batching/caching settings with their team.

Attachments: careoptics-initial-poc-requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet with fields they provided on the call).

Can you draft the initial numbers by Tue EOD so I can share with Tom before the kickoff? If you want a quick sync, 11am PDT Mon works for me.

Thanks,
Jasmine

I'll also call out the VPC/KMS items (should be fine but may need our infra team to provision private endpoints). Will aim to have the ask back to you by Tue EOD.
